target: SWE intern / new-grad roles (general software engineering, 2026–27 recruiting cycle)
seven_second_takeaway: UMD CS '28, AWS SDE intern now, Capital One SWE intern; heavy AWS/LLM backend work, research lab, campus studio. Strong brands, but lots of concurrent roles.

score_rationale.impact_clarity: Several bullets stop at the method (Fargate/CDK deploy, PhysTwin, all IEX bullets) with no stated result or user-visible outcome.
score_rationale.quantification: Percentages lack sample size or baseline (90% surveyed, 93% testers, 30% setup); Prisma/Redis caching claims reduced load with no number.
score_rationale.concision_readability: Nearly every bullet runs a full two lines with stacked tech names; dense to read, few short wins break it up.
score_rationale.skim_test: AWS and Capital One pop, but headline wins are buried mid-sentence; a one-line AWS bullet leads the section.
score_rationale.credibility: Summer 2026 shows Capital One, IEX project, contract job and research lab concurrently; 'adopted into ecosystem' and 'enforced correctness' invite hard follow-ups.

must_fix: Clarify the overlap: Jun–Aug 2026 lists Capital One (Richmond) plus IEX project, UMD contracting and UMIACS (College Park) all active; an interviewer will ask how many hours each got.
Clarify: what does 'adopted into Leo's ecosystem' concretely mean (who uses it, in what capacity)? As written it reads as puffery.
Clarify: is Tortuga the class scheduler? The bullet pairs a caching change with a traffic number, implying causation that isn't there.
Clarify sample sizes for '90% of surveyed users' and '93% ... internal testers'; small-n percentages collapse under one question.
